scan.matching: Each file is read as bytes. A primitive is listed for a file when its token pattern matches the lower-cased bytes at an accepted position or one of its wrapper symbols occurs as a whole identifier. A position is accepted unless the byte before it is in `not_preceded_by`; with `camel_case` a match that starts with an upper-case letter directly after a lower-case letter or digit is accepted as well. A wrapper symbol is a case-sensitive pattern, optionally limited to paths, anchored on the definition that reaches the primitive. A file-granularity unit records the primitive set of every file; a tree-granularity unit records one primitive set for all its files.
scan.exclude_reason: The checker, its reference modules and its tests name every primitive as data. They are still scanned for pinned commitment values and commitment types.

tree_unit_overrides.reason: Third-party sources vendored for patches and test oracles; their digests are those of the upstream projects.

The KAGEMUSHA offline monetary-authority product is outside the ZK delivery plan. Its files inside the proof and primitive-owner crates are recorded per file under the consumer `kagemusha`, because they share the Halo2, Pasta Poseidon and BN254 owners; its files elsewhere are recorded as one set.

Its primitive set is recorded as one set even inside a proof crate.

scope.tree_unit_default: Every other scanned file belongs to the tree unit `<package>#other`, where the package is `crates/<name>` or the top-level directory.
scope.file_unit: A path under a listed prefix belongs to the file-granularity unit `<package>#zk`, unless a tree-unit override that applies inside the proof crates matches it. A path under one of the path roots belongs to that unit when its lower-cased form matches the pattern or the file names one of `file_granularity_primitives`, unless a tree-unit override matches it. Tooling directories (scripts, xtask, ci, tools, pytests, examples) are always tree units.

producer_ledger.method: Lexical (scripts/zk_rust_lexical_index.py). A function is listed when its body, without nested functions, matches a detector. A file is production when a chain of `mod` declarations without a test attribute reaches it from the crate root; a function is test-only when a test attribute guards it or an enclosing block. Domain literals are the printable string literals of the body and of the constants of the same file that the body names.
producer_ledger.limits: A function that only forwards to a listed producer is not listed. A digest reached through a macro or through a constant of another file has no domain literal here. Test-only producers are counted per file, not listed.

decision_rule: If every changing role accepts a generic quantum collision estimate near 85 bits, the canonical native commitment is raw BLAKE3-256.

If any changing role requires at least 128 bits against quantum collision search, that role, or all of them for uniformity, uses an analysed 384-bit sponge: SHAKE256 with 48 bytes of output over the same frame. The tree already holds a byte-framed SHA3-384 owner for the privacy STARK substrate.

GoldilocksDigest384V1 is not the native default: it is slower natively by orders of magnitude and specs/fastpq_compact_digest_security.md records it as unqualified. It stays only where a Goldilocks relation recomputes it.
The existing 48-byte wire width is not a reason to keep a digest.

A digest that is recomputed inside a relation keeps a native-field algebraic hash; every bridge between a native commitment and an in-circuit digest is specified explicitly, and an unconstrained native digest is never treated as equal to the bytes it commits to.

A native commitment whose value is a domain field, a seed or a public input of a proof moves only in the same cutover as that proof profile (decision `changes-with-profile`); the transcript-seed check of each role records which case holds.

security_rationale.estimates: Ideal-hash estimates, not qualification claims: 128 bits against classical collision search, about 85 bits against quantum collision search (Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp), 256 bits against classical and 128 bits against quantum preimage search.
security_rationale.labels: A composition is labelled by its weakest property. A protocol labelled pq-qrom that relies on collision resistance of a 256-bit commitment is not a 128-bit post-quantum composition; H.2 either accepts the lower estimate in the label or selects the 384-bit sponge for that role.
security_rationale.framing: Domain separation comes from the frame, not from keyed or derive-key modes, so every SDK needs only the unkeyed hash.
security_rationale.review_state: BLAKE3 inherits the analysis of BLAKE2 with a reduced round count; SHAKE256 is FIPS 202. Neither statement is a review of this composition.

cost_rationale.summary: A byte-oriented digest is one compression call per 64 bytes with vector implementations on every supported platform; the six-lane algebraic digest runs 6 x 65 field rounds for every 14 input bytes.
cost_rationale.exploratory_measurement: See exploratory_measurements; single machine, single run, guidance only.
cost_rationale.in_circuit: The candidate is never opened in a relation, so it adds no constraint cost. A role that later needs an in-circuit opening leaves the candidate (see provisional).

bn254_poseidon.construction: Original Poseidon (not Poseidon2) over the BN254 scalar field: x^5, dense Cauchy MDS, widths 3 (rate 2) and 6 (rate 5), 8 full and 56 partial rounds for both widths, first Cauchy candidate (secure_mds = 0).
method: The reference script regenerates all 621 field elements with its own Grain LFSR and Cauchy construction and compares them with the Rust table.

The same generator run with the published round numbers reproduces pinned constants of the published BN254 width-three instantiation, so the generator is anchored to published values and not only to the repository table.
Every square minor of both matrices is checked, with three bounded linear-layer screens for one active S-box per partial round.
The paper's round-number inequalities for x^5 at a 128-bit target are evaluated with the objective of the fewest S-boxes and the margin of two full rounds and 7.5% partial rounds.
The Rust test runs the owner over vectors the script computed with its own permutation.
bn254_poseidon.limits: Agreement of two implementations, nonzero minors and the bounded screens do not qualify the parameter set. The inequalities are transcribed from the paper; the original round-number script was not fetched. Parameters are not changed by this task.

defects.title: The width-three table is not the published BN254 instantiation
defects.evidence: The published BN254 x^5 width-three permutation (hadeshash poseidonperm_x5_254_3, also shipped as the bn256 parameters of the poseidon-primitives 0.2.0 test oracle) uses 57 partial rounds. The repository uses 56. The Grain seed binds the round count, so none of the 195 published round constants and none of the MDS entries equal the repository's. The repository's value satisfies the margin rule as evaluated here (minimum 56).
defects.effect: Outputs differ from every other BN254 Poseidon deployment that follows the published instantiation; no attack follows from the round count.

defects.title: The width-six round count is one partial round below the margin rule
defects.evidence: For width 6 the inequalities need 53 partial rounds with 6 full rounds; the margin gives 8 full and 57 partial rounds. The repository uses 8 and 56. This is the result of the transcribed inequalities, not of the fetched reference script, and it is not a demonstrated attack. No published BN254 width-six instantiation exists to compare constants with.
defects.effect: The width-six permutation has less than the recommended margin.

defects.title: The two- and six-input helpers are single permutations without capacity or domain separation
defects.evidence: hash2 starts from the state [a, b, 0] and hash6 fills all six state coordinates with inputs; both return coordinate 0 of one permutation. hash6 has no capacity element: for unrestricted field inputs a collision is found by inverting the permutation, so its collision resistance rests on every caller and every circuit restricting the inputs to 64-bit values. hash2_u64 and hash6_u64 return only the low 64 bits. Neither helper shares a domain word with the byte sponge.
defects.effect: A consumer that treats these helpers as general collision-resistant hashes over field elements, or the 64-bit forms as commitments, has a weaker guarantee than its label.

grinding: A profile with nonzero grinding binds a nonce whose predicate covers the whole preceding transcript, at one frozen difficulty. A profile with zero grinding bits has no nonce and claims no work-security term.

A difficulty of d bits costs about 2^d classical hash evaluations and about 2^(d/2) quantum oracle steps under idealized search; neither figure is a soundness bound, and work-security is accounted separately from algebraic and FRI error.
The nonce width and the search bound are fixed, so a prover cannot grind across statement variants.

The exact mapping of a concrete transcript remains necessary; until it is supplied the claim stays open and the label is not pq-qrom on the strength of the hash alone.

profiles.name: lantern.trapdoor.falcon512-derived.v1
profiles.summary: Disposition of PQ-D3: the issuer trapdoor of Bootle Lantern is frozen as what the tree implements, a Falcon-512-derived NTRU trapdoor with arbitrary-target preimage sampling under fixed sampling caps and a mandatory equation and norm check. It is not FN-DSA and not a signature scheme.
profiles.typed_owner_pending: The engine binds its own descriptor string today. F.5 with P.13 derives this identity from typed code, records the vendored provenance in a source-checked inventory and adds upstream and adaptation-specific known answers.

security.basis: The NTRU trapdoor, key generation and Gaussian sampling follow the round-three Falcon-512 design; the adaptation changes the target, the output and the sampling bounds.
security.not_established: FN-DSA conformance (FIPS 206 is not final); the full Lantern security reduction; known answers for arbitrary-target preimages, sampling caps and exhaustion. Round-three signature vectors alone do not cover the adaptation.

binding_order.bound: The complete typed profile descriptor (construction, framing, primitives, field and encodings, domains, masking bounds, out-of-domain claims, DEEP composition, FRI schedule, sampling rules, message schedule, grinding, proof frame, declared envelope), the catalog, and the statement context (relation identity, public-column layout, geometry, complete statement).
binding_order.how: They form the prefix frame that begins every SHA3-256 and every SHAKE256 input, including the first leaf and the first tape. The statement carries the relation's public IO, State anchors, execution context and replay domain; its completeness is the relation owner's obligation.

binding_order.bound: The row root of the 301 retained trace columns.
binding_order.how: Chained with the whole first tape before the 923 constraint coefficients are derived.

binding_order.bound: The joined root of both quotient chunks and the composition mask.
All 604 out-of-domain answers, every coordinate, in current-row, next-row, quotient order.
binding_order.how: Hashed as one leaf and chained before the batching scalar.

binding_order.bound: Each of the five FRI layer roots.
binding_order.how: Chained before its own folding challenge.

binding_order.bound: The complete terminal: the root of the single leaf holding all 128 values. The profile has zero grinding bits, so no nonce exists.
The complete bounded openings and their indices.
binding_order.how: The verifier derives every index from the query tape, authenticates each opened row, quotient leaf, fiber and the whole terminal against the committed roots under the same prefix, and rejects a missing, extra, reordered or altered opening.

shared_transcript.invariant: No challenge is derived before the commitments it tests: a changed commitment changes every later tape and no earlier one.
domain_separation: SHA3-256 and SHAKE256 are separated by their FIPS 202 suffixes.
Leaves, parents, chain commitments and tapes are separated by the body kind; oracles by tag and round; positions by level and index; the requested output length is part of every body.
Statements, relations and profiles are separated by the complete prefix; no digest of the context replaces its bytes.
sampling: A tape is materialized once at its fixed extent. A word at or above the modulus is rejected, never reduced, and no rejection squeezes another byte.
Rejected and unused words are part of the whole tape that the next chain commitment binds.
A base-field out-of-domain point, exhaustion, a wrong phase and a malformed message abort the attempt permanently.
The query tape must first yield all 87 accepted candidates; the first 77 distinct positions are used in ascending order.

grinding.statement: The profile has zero grinding bits and the proof frame has no nonce field. No work-security term is claimed. The requirement to bind a nonce before the query positions applies only to a profile with nonzero grinding.
grinding.open: B.2 counts repeated attempts and prover-controlled variation of statements and commitments in the adversary budget: permanent abort prevents further sampling inside one attempt, not adversarial retries.

work_limits.bound: The profile's declared envelope: the relation identity, statement, context and frame byte ceilings, the decoder allocation, sequence and nesting bounds, the layer, path and fiber bounds, and the structural work charge with the version and unit of its accounting.
work_limits.not_bound: Caller ceilings (WorkLimits, VerifierLimits, ProducerLimits values). They are admission policy and must not change proof bytes; admission enforces committed-State policy separately, and the limit types alone do not show that a caller took its ceilings from State.
work_limits.structural_work_charge: 29,751 units is a structural charge of a maximal frame under accounting version 1, not complete verification work. Complete resource accounting is B.2 and F.2 work.

security_statement.status: Transcript semantics are frozen. Security qualification of the q77 profile is pending and no numerical error is established.
security_statement.claim_form: Any claim is an absolute error at a stated query budget, stated separately for the classical and the quantum random-oracle model. No work-normalized 128-bit claim is made.
security_statement.commitments: SHA3-256: generic collision search costs about 2^128 classical work and about 2^85 quantum queries (Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp); preimage search about 2^256 classical and 2^128 quantum. These are ideal-hash estimates.
security_statement.challenges: SHAKE256 with a 512-bit capacity; each verifier message is one oracle output of its exact extent.
security_statement.classical_rom: Conditional. It needs a round-by-round soundness bound for the actual q77 interactive oracle proof (blowup 128, arities 16, 16, 8, 8, 4, degree bound 2N, 77 queries, masked DEEP composition) and the mapping of this chained transcript and its Merkle commitments to the BCS compilation. Neither exists in the tree: the reviewed round-by-round argument is for the retired q375 binary profile. B.2 owns the exact-geometry reduction and the checked accounting.
security_statement.qrom: Open. In Chiesa-Manohar-Spooner, ordinary round-by-round soundness supports the modified chain that contains the verifier messages; the stronger property of their section 8.6 concerns original BCS messages generated outside the chain. The exact mapping of the q77 transcript to that compiler, with its query accounting, remains necessary and is not supplied.
security_statement.hiding: Only the honest-verifier algebraic answer view is argued (specs/fastpq_deep_hiding_construction.md). The adaptive Merkle and Fiat-Shamir simulator is open.
security_statement.algebraic_error: Algebraic and FRI error sums alone establish neither Fiat-Shamir soundness nor hiding.
security_statement.tests_establish: Implementation conformance with the frozen binding, not soundness.
security_statement.invalidation: A change of any descriptor parameter, including a query count or a FRI schedule that B.2's accounting requires, changes the identity and makes every measurement that names the previous identity inapplicable. No reviewer token is involved.

measurement_binding.rule: Every workload names the profiles it depends on (`profiles`) and the selections it still waits for (`profiles_not_frozen`). A measurement inside a workload has `measurement_scope: workload-profiles` and names the exact complete workload profile set in `profile_identities`; an omitted identity cannot evade invalidation. Only the canonical-native candidate comparison section accepts `measurement_scope: bare-primitives`, with an empty identity map and an explanatory `scope_note`; that comparison describes no frozen frame profile. The owning section fixes the scope, never a measurement's free-text explanation. A measurement that names an identity other than the current one of that profile is inapplicable: the check fails until it is re-measured or moved to `inapplicable_measurements` with the identity it was taken under.
measurement_binding.final_measurements: H.3 measures only workloads whose `profiles_not_frozen` is empty, and binds each record to these identities through the profile field of the measurement identity.
measurement_binding.harness_field: A workload's `profile_set_identity` is the SHA3-256 of `iroha:semantic-profile-set:v1`, a zero byte, the profile count as a u32 little-endian and the 32-byte identities of its `profiles` in order (fastpq_isi::semantic_profile::semantic_profile_set_id_v1). A measurement record of crates/iroha_measurement names it in the `profile` field of its identity as `semantic=<profile_set_identity>+<build profile>`, which is within the identity text grammar of crates/iroha_measurement/src/text.rs.
measurement_binding.no_reviewer_token: Invalidation is a comparison of identities by the check. No signature, approval or runtime switch is involved.
